Subject Alleged proposals made by Mr. Sun Fo during his recent trip to
Moscow and alleged counter proposals submitted by Soviet Russia.

Made by .................... and .................... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Referring to a report in the Shanghai Daily News
dated March 25, 1938, enquiries made amongst ex-Government
officials have failed to confirm the report that Mr. Sun Fo
had ever been authorised to discuss the conclusion of a
military pact between China and Soviet Russia and the
introduction of an equal number of communists into government
service.

From observations kept on the developments of
the conference at Hankow, there appears to have no indication
of an expansion of communist influence in the Kuomintang and
the appointment of General Chiang Kai Shek to the leadership
of the Kuomintang seems to have received the support of
communists and dispelled all rumours of a split between the
Kuomintang and the Communists.

March 25, 1938. Afternoon Translation. SPECI

Shanghai Daily News (上海日报), a mosquito paper, publishes
the following telegram from Hongkong :-

SINO-SOVIET UNDERSTANDING OVER SUPPLY OF WAR
MATERIALS

The negotiations conducted by Mr. Sun
Fo, President of the Legislative Yuan of the National
Government, during his recent trip to Moscow have been
kept strictly confidential, but it is learnt that they
had reference to the following matters:-
(1) The conclusion of a military pact
between China and Soviet Russia including Outer Mongolia.
(2) Negotiations for a loan for the
construction of a railway and a motor road connecting
North-west China with Soviet Russia.
(3) To enter into a definite under-
standing with the Soviet Government over the question
of the supply of arms and munitions and aviators to
China.

It is reported that M. Stalin is in
favour of these three proposals and has offered the
following conditions:-
(1) In view of the fact that co-operation
now exists between the Kuomintang and the Communist
Party, the latter should be given equal rights in the
government. Consequently, the two sides should have an
equal number of seats on the Military Affairs Commission
and in the various departments of the Executive Yuan.
(2) A joint committee should be
established by China, Soviet Russia and Outer Mongolia
to decide upon plans of reconstruction. The committee
will consist of eleven members, of whom the Chinese
Government will appoint 6, the Moscow Government 4 and
Outer Mongolia 1.
(3) 50% of the firearms supplied by
Soviet Russia should be allotted to the 8th Route Army.
The monthly supply of arms and
munitions to China from the U.S.S.R. will be 15 tanks,
15 aeroplanes, 65 heavy machine guns, etc.
Nothing is known of the final outcome
of these negotiations, but it is generally believed that
it will be impossible for the time being for the Chinese
Government to accept the first and the third counter-
demands submitted by the Soviet Government.

Subject Reported conclusion of a Sino-Soviet Agreement.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [签名]

In compliance with instructions of the Deputy
Commissioner (Special Branch) regarding the possible conclusion
of a Sino-Soviet Agreement, I have to report that following
the occupation of Mukden by Japan on September 18, 1931,
the National Government became aware of the ever encroaching
policy of its eastern neighbour - Japan, and the necessity
of cultivating good relations with other nations for the
maintenance of peace in the Far East. Emissaries have,
therefore, been appointed to the various foreign Powers
ostensibly to investigate economic and social problems,
but with the real object of obtaining international
co-operation in regard to the development of China which
should precede an effective resistance against foreign
invasion. In order to cope with any emergency that may
arise, China has at the same time been engaged in economical
and social reforms, and the military training of the populace
throughout the country.

Owing to the present impasse existing between
China and Japan, rumours have been current to the effect
that China and the U.S.S.R. have concluded an agreement.
Although it is impossible to obtain any concrete confirmation
of this report, the consensus of opinion is that there is
a likelihood of an agreement between the Soviet Union and
China being reached and that the public announcement of
such a pact being temporarily shelved for diplomatic reasons.

According to unconfirmed information from independent
sources, the negotiations, for the conclusion of an agreement
with the U.S.S.R., were originally conducted by Mr. Chen
Koo-fu, present Chairman of the Kiangsu Provincial

Subject Appointment of Mr. Er Hsieh Sung (欧学底), Nanking Political Agent,
to succeed Li Kuo Kan.

Made by....................and....................Forwarded by....Supt.. Tan Shao-liang..

(批：Radio
L. 50/2)

Referring to report dated July 11, 1930, re the
indifference displayed by the Nanking political agent, Li Kuo
Kan, during the past eight months or so, Mr. Li called at this
office this morning introducing his successor, Mr. Er Hsieh (欧学底)
Sung, and stating that his repeated request to resign from the
present post has been accepted by Nanking.

He gives as the reason for his quitting Shanghai that
he has been too long in this line of service which he joined
about 18 months ago and accordingly he desired to be relieved
of his duties. He adds that his successor will continue the
campaign against Communists as before.

Questioned regarding a report of some understanding
having been reached between the Nanking and Soviet Governments,
Mr. Li refused to discuss the matter. He, however, admits
Mr. Chang Chun, who has been to Moscow on a mission from the
Government, has returned.

(印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER
17 AUG
CRIME BRANCH)

Mr. Er Hsieh Sung, the successor, is a student of the
Whampoa Academy. He served with the 1st Division in Hunan
under General Ho Yao Chu for three years. He then proceeded
to Kansu with the anti-Communist punitive expedition.

Returning to Nanking recently, he joined the Central
Tangpu and was instructed by the latter to take up the new
post. Whether his enthusiasm over the hunting down of Communists
will be the same as his former colleagues, remains to be seen.

Tan Shao-liang
Superintendent.

Subject Departure of Mr. Chang Chun (张冲) for Moscow.

Made by .................... and .................... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

An important member of the Central Tangpu in the
course of conversation on July 10 revealed the fact that
Mr. Chang Chun, a returned student from Russia, at present
member of the C.E.C., recently left for Moscow on a very
important mission from General Chiang Kai Shek the nature of
which although not yet disclosed, has probably something to do
with joint defense measures against Japan. Mr. Chang was
accompanied by a Russian woman who is his "second" wife.
It is learnt that he has made two visits to Russia
prior to the recent one. This may account for the explanation
why the Nanking political agent in Shanghai has been unusually
quiet during the past six months or so.

Tan Shao-liang
Superintendent.

NIPPO (Tientsin, Nov.2.)

ANTI-JAPANESE UNIVERSITY TO BE ESTABLISHED WITH
SOVIET ASSISTANCE

Public attention has already
been attracted to the character of the Russo-Chinese
Secret Military Agreement.

On November 1 a prospectus was
issued in the name of the "National Salvation and anti-
Japanese University" inviting students to enrol. This
university is reported to be located in the northern
part of Shensi Province; it was established with the
assistance of Soviet Russia. It will educate anti-Japanese
students.

The other day Mr. Sun Fo
delivered the following speech:-"An anti-Japanese movement
is the only way to increase China's power. The power of
the National Government and its people is not strong
enough at present and Soviet Russia's co-operation is
necessary."

Soviet Russia is now rendering
every assistance to the anti-Japanese movement in China
in order to recover the popular front which has sustained
a reverse in Spain and France.

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK CARRYING OUT RUSSO-CHINESE
SECRET MILITARY AGREEMENT

Tientsin, October 31.
It has been ascertained that
General Chiang Kai Shek is at present actively engaged in
preparing for a war against Japan. He is now carrying
out the terms of the Russo-Chinese Secret Military
Agreement concluded in March, 1936.
The agreement contains the
following terms:-
1. China shall permit the Red Army to enter the
North-West. The Nanking Government agrees to suspend its
operations against the Red Army.
2. The Red Army agrees not to establish any independent
state in Chinese territory in order to protect China's
territorial integrity.
3. The Red Army and the Nanking Government Army under
the control of General Chiang Kai Shek will form a joint
anti-Japanese front.
4. China and Soviet Russia will do their utmost to
improve their relations.
5. An anti-Japanese war should be waged in December.
China and Russia will present a united front.

NIPPO

KASHING AUTHORITIES TREAT CHINESE DEALING IN JAPANESE
GOODS AS TRAITOR

On October 25 a certain Chinese
named Wu, an employee of the Shintoku Dental Apparatus Co.
on Tientsin Road, Shanghai, which is owned by a Formosan
named Sai Sei Ki, was arrested by the Bureau of Public
Safety at Kashing for selling Japanese dental apparatus
and his goods were seized. On October 29 he was handed
over to the Headquarters of the Peace Preservation Corps
at Kashing on a charge of being a traitor. On October
31 Mr. Sai Sei Ki, the employer of the Chinese, reported
the incident to the Japanese authorities. The Japanese
Consuls at Hangchow and at Nanking will open negotiations
with the Chekiang Provincial authorities for the release
of the Chinese.
